definitions.explanation: A person who follows and serves a leader or boss figure. Originally from the hierarchical oyabun-kobun (boss-follower) system, now used more broadly for any loyal underling.

examples.japanese: {親分|おやぶん}と{子分|こぶん}の{関係|かんけい}。
{彼|かれ}はいつもボスの{子分|こぶん}のように{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}う。
examples.english: He always acts like the boss's henchman.

examples.japanese: ガキ{大将|たいしょう}は{子分|こぶん}を{引|ひ}き{連|つ}れて{公園|こうえん}にやってきた。
examples.english: The neighborhood bully came to the park with his gang of followers.

notes:
Comes from the traditional Japanese {親分|おやぶん}・{子分|こぶん} (boss-follower) hierarchy, which originated in feudal loyalty structures and is strongly associated with yakuza organizations. In modern usage, it is also used colloquially or humorously for any boss-underling dynamic, including among children.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {親分|おやぶん}と{子分|こぶん}: boss and follower (paired set)
- {子分|こぶん}になる: to become someone's follower
- {子分|こぶん}を{従|したが}える: to have followers in tow
- {子分|こぶん}{肌|はだ}: having the temperament of a follower

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {部下|ぶか}: subordinate — workplace term; professional and neutral
- {手下|てした}: underling — somewhat derogatory; implies being used
- {弟子|でし}: disciple, apprentice — implies a teaching relationship

cross_references.label: younger-brother figure, junior (in a close relationship)
